scenario: [LEXP.6.2]: `len` raises a TypeError if the `Json` value isn't an array, and a path that does not resolve reads as `null` ([LNUL.8.4]), which is not an array either -- so `len` of it is the TypeError, and `has` is the guard the clause names for such a path. The formal tie says so outright: formal/idris/Rete/Eval.idr `lexp_6_1__len` and `lexp_6_2__len_is_an_arrays_alone` give a trap for every object, every scalar leaf, and `null`. The twin of LEXP.6.2.len_of_a_non_array_is_a_type_error, for the path that resolves to nothing rather than to an object: `body` has no `missing` key. A runtime that answers `null` there records no fault, and `null == 0` does not fire, so the event sequence is empty; this vector requires the `type_error`. Path: libds builtins.c `builtin_json_len` (found == NULL), Mercury ds.eval.m `json_introspect` (the unresolved arm).
